Crispy Honey-Garlic Chicken Thighs

It was the autumn my grandmother first took me to the county fair, and the leaves were doing that thing where they turn the color of, well, honey-garlic chicken. I remember the hayrides. I remember the pumpkins. Mostly I remember thinking, one day I will write four thousand words about this before sharing a recipe.

My husband Dave (you'll remember Dave from the sourdough saga of 2019, and the Great Pickle Incident, and honestly every third paragraph on this blog) took one bite of these thighs and said, and I quote, "these are thighs." He's a man of few words. The dog, Biscuit, agreed, in the sense that she stared at the pan for forty-five straight minutes.

Now, a lot of people ask me: what is the secret to crispy skin? And I always say: patience, a hot oven, and reading another six paragraphs of my musings first. Did you know honey has been harvested for over eight thousand years? Fascinating. Anyway, here are three hundred more words about garlic varieties, my trip to a garlic festival, and a poll about whether you, the reader, prefer your garlic minced or crushed.
